title: Follow existing repository design conventions
summary: Before implementing or refactoring code, inspect existing patterns and design conventions in the repository and align with them rather than improvising ad-hoc designs.
strategy: Inspect existing sibling implementations and callers in the target module before writing new code.
Follow established parameter patterns, helper abstractions, and separation of concerns rather than overloading existing parameters or improvising ad-hoc flags.
Verify new changes match the surrounding architecture before finalizing.
author: JiaqiZhang-Dev

title: Write docs as current state
summary: Document the current state directly without narrating intermediate progress or past decisions.
strategy: Write features and usage in the present tense as the current state.
Omit intermediate progress, past decisions, and stale terminology.
author: JiaqiZhang-Dev

title: Keep changes minimal unless refactoring is necessary
summary: Keep code changes minimal and surgical; avoid unnecessary refactoring unless strictly required.
strategy: Make the smallest surgical change that solves the issue without touching unrelated code or signatures.
Avoid speculative refactoring unless it is strictly required for correctness or explicitly requested.
author: JiaqiZhang-Dev

title: Do not hard-wrap lines in Markdown docs
summary: Write Markdown paragraphs and list items without hard-wrapping lines across all repositories.
strategy: Keep each Markdown paragraph or list item on a single line without manual line breaks.
Disable or avoid automatic line-wrapping formatting in documentation edits across all repositories.
author: JiaqiZhang-Dev

title: Follow TCGC reuse, caching, and testing conventions
summary: TCGC development conventions verified during PR #5837: reuse built-in decorator scope, TCGCContext caching, compiler traversal, and dist-backed test/doc workflows with minimal diffs.
strategy: Store and read scoped decorator data with setScopedDecoratorData and getScopedDecoratorData instead of custom stateMap or scope parsers.
Keep per-run caches on TCGCContext (checking .has() when undefined is cached) and resolve semantics inside the existing type pass rather than adding extra loops or module-level caches.
Reuse compiler helpers like walkPropertiesInherited and existing diagnostics/rule judgment rather than extracting single-use wrappers or duplicating validation.

Run pnpm --filter @azure-tools/typespec-client-generator-core build before Vitest because createTester loads compiled JS from dist/, and run regen-docs after editing decorator or diagnostic docs without hard-wrapping Markdown lines.
solution: Reuse TCGC scoped decorator helpers, TCGCContext caches, existing type passes, compiler traversal utilities, and build dist before running Vitest tester suites.
author: JiaqiZhang-Dev

title: Reuse TCGC scoped decorator helpers
summary: Reuse TCGC's built-in scoped decorator helpers and metadata-only decorator pattern instead of reimplementing scope parsing or testing standard scope behavior.
strategy: Store and read scoped decorator data with setScopedDecoratorData and getScopedDecoratorData rather than custom stateMap or scope parsers.
Use metadata-only decorators with createSdkContext's additionalDecorators and getTypeDecorators when emitters only need filtered metadata.
Omit redundant tests for standard decorator scope precedence.
solution: Reuse setScopedDecoratorData/getScopedDecoratorData and additionalDecorators instead of custom scope logic or redundant scope tests.
author: JiaqiZhang-Dev
